items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the mental hygiene law, in relation to adding siblings to the definition of a "qualified person"
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S2933

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the mental hygiene law, in relation
to adding siblings to the definition of a "qualified person"

 PURPOSE :

In addition to a parent, spouse, or adult child of a person with a
developmental disability this legislation would add sibling of an
adult patient to the list of individuals entitled to request access to
clinical records.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section one states that a "qualified person" is a guardian of a person
with a developmental disability with access to clinical records of
such individual. The list of individuals entitled to access include a
parent, spouse, and adult child. Siblings of an adult patient would be
added to this section.

Section two states that this act shall take effect immediately.

 JUSTIFICATION :

Currently in Mental Health law a "qualified person" with access to
clinical records of a person with a developmental disability includes
the patient or client, guardian, parent, spouse, or adult child. This
list should be expanded to include siblings. Siblings often play an
essential role in the primary care of a developmentally disabled
family member.

In 2007, Jonathon's Law was established to ensure that families would
have access to information on the care and treatment of their
children. In keeping with the intent of Jonathan's Law, the addition
of siblings within the definition of "qualified person" would ensure
access to records which are crucial when an incidence of abuse has
been alleged.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

2015-16: S.7804 Passed Senate/Referred to Mental Health

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately.

BILL NUMBER:  S2933A

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the mental hygiene law, in relation
to adding adult siblings to those who may have access to clinical
records

 PURPOSE :

In addition to a parent, spouse, or adult child of a person with a
developmental disability this legislation would add an adult sibling
of an adult patient to the list of individuals entitled to request
access to clinical records.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section one amends the definition of "qualified person" within the
mental hygiene law to include adult siblings

Section two of the bill makes corresponding amendments to subdivision
(b) of section 33.16 of the mental hygiene law to identify adult
siblings' authority to access clinical records

Section three establishes the effective date

 JUSTIFICATION :

clinical records of a person with a developmental disability includes
the patient or client, guardian, parent, spouse, or adult child. This
list should be expanded to include adult siblings. Adult siblings
often play an essential role in the primary care of a developmentally
disabled family member.

In 2007, Jonathon's Law was established to ensure that families would
have access to information on the care and treatment of their
children. In keeping with the intent of Jonathan's Law, the addition
of adult siblings within the definition of "qualified person" would
ensure access to records which are crucial when an incidence of abuse
has been alleged.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

2015-16: S.7804 Passed Senate/Referred to Mental Health

None.

This act shall take effect immediately.
